A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnyBCQ work, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. v1 ends after the references; v2 adds Appendix A.1–A.5. The supplied material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream accuracy, kernel latency, perplexity, and end-to-end throughput measurements in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original summarization, perplexity, kernel profiling, H100 throughput, and power measurements in Table 5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, progressive precision expansion, shared binary planes, per-precision scale optimization, and the kernel procedure remain unchanged. Section 5 applies the existing framework within PMPD decoding without specifying a new quantization or kernel algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds CNN/DailyMail abstractive summarization with precision varying during generation, substantially extending the evaluated tasks beyond v1's knowledge, commonsense, and perplexity tests. Appendix A.1 also evaluates C4 perplexity; v1 used C4 only for calibration.

E2.justification: ShiftAddLLM joins the accuracy–throughput comparison across all three models in Figure 4. In v1 it appeared in Table 2's accuracy comparison but not Figure 4. Comparator membership in the existing Tables 2–4 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The original Section 4.1 settings are retained. Added experiments introduce mixed-precision decoding at average bit-widths 3.6, 3.15, and 2.23 with ROUGE-L and BERTScore, H100 throughput testing, clock64() kernel instrumentation, and power/utilization sampling every 100 ms over 10 seconds. These are additional protocols, not documented revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds fixed-versus-multi-precision perplexity comparisons, operation-level latency breakdowns, tests of throughput gains across GPU generations, and power/memory characterization. Section 5 and Appendix A.5 add a mixed-precision generation case study and failure examples. These substantially extend v1's fixed-precision accuracy control and aggregate performance comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, independent repeat counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix A.1 attributes small differences to evaluation noise without quantifying uncertainty. Appendix A.4's temporal sampling and averaging document a measurement protocol, not between-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values, while Tables 5–9 and Figure 4 add substantial results. For example, Table 5 reports ROUGE-L of 0.178 for AnyBCQ versus 0.154 for Any-Precision LLM at average precision 3.6. Figure 4 also changes the plotted Llama-3.1-8B 2-bit AnyBCQ accuracy from approximately 0.35 to 0.30, although Table 4 still reports 0.3532; this is an unexplained reporting discrepancy.

T1.justification: The BCQ representation, residual definitions, least-squares expressions, and precision parameterization remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or new derivation is added. Section 6's acknowledgment of missing theoretical guarantees is a limitation statement.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and summary retain the same claims about shared bit-planes, progressive precision expansion, low-bit accuracy, and hardware efficiency, including the same headline throughput gains. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about missing theoretical guarantees and explains small fixed-versus-multi-precision reversals as evaluation noise. It also interprets repetitive generation as a low-bit failure, discusses transfer across GPU generations, and predicts larger gains on specialized accelerators. The existing shared-binary representational limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a code-repository address and a reproducibility statement describing supplementary quantization code, evaluation pipelines, CUDA benchmarking scripts, and execution instructions. Appendices A.2 and A.4 document instrumentation and sampling procedures. This substantially expands reported reproducibility resources while retaining the original hyperparameters; the external resources themselves are not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ROUGE and BERTScore, removes Wei et al. (2022) and ZeroQuant, and clarifies the optimization differences between AnyBCQ and ShiftAddLLM. Discussion of the already-cited PMPD and DP-LLM is expanded, while the central positioning relative to BCQ and Any-Precision LLM remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally rewritten, and the memory-footprint discussion moves from the methodology into the introduction. Case-study, discussion, reproducibility, and appendix sections are added, alongside header and terminology edits. Most retained prose and the method narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: New Tables 5–9 provide displays for generation quality, perplexity, latency components, cross-GPU throughput, and hardware measurements. Figure 4 is redrawn with ShiftAddLLM markers, an expanded legend, and adjusted axes. Table 1 and existing figures are relocated, while several table headers and layouts are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The added perplexity controls, kernel profiling, and H100 measurements strengthen support for the unchanged contribution, while code-access and measurement documentation improve reproducibility information. However, the generation study omits important model and decoding details, Appendix A.5 Example 2 pairs outputs on different topics, and revised Figure 4 conflicts with unchanged Table 4. The useful validation outweighs these reporting regressions, but the overall gain is limited.
